claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in high-entropy alloys is governed by formation of a protective surface layer.
Mo addition enhances formation of the protective surface layer.
Si addition enhances formation of the protective surface layer.
The cocktail effect influences protective-surface-layer formation.
Elemental additions can refine the grains of a high-entropy alloy.
Si addition can improve the wear resistance of a high-entropy alloy.
Adding Mo and Si will enhance resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion relative to an alloy without those additions.
Adding Mo and Si will reduce wear rate by at least 20% relative to the baseline.
Adding Mo and Si will increase corrosion resistance by at least 15% relative to the baseline.
The prediction applies to high-entropy alloys containing Mo and Si in harsh corrosive mechanical environments.
The exact mechanism of protective-layer formation and its relationship to grain refinement and the cocktail effect is not fully understood.
A controlled comparison should use high-entropy alloys with and without Mo and Si additions under the same harsh corrosive mechanical environment.
The hypothesis is falsified if wear rate and corrosion resistance are not significantly different from baseline at p < 0.05.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies improvements of at least 20% in wear rate and 15% in corrosion resistance, but the falsification rule rejects the hypothesis only when differences are statistically nonsignificant. A smaller yet statistically significant improvement would violate the quantitative prediction without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
